questions.question: How can you help prevent rollovers?

options.text: Speed up quickly after stopping.
Drive slowly around turns.
Place the load near the back of the trailer.
Place the load on one side of the trailer.

questions.explanation: To prevent rollovers, keep your load low and centered. Take all curves and corners slowly.

questions.question: When you couple glad hands, at what angle should the seals be pressed together?

options.text: 30 degrees.
45 degrees.
60 degrees.
90 degrees.

questions.explanation: When coupling glad hands, press the seals together at a 90-degree angle.

questions.question: In a double or triple combination, how should you position the trailers?

options.text: Spread the cargo weight evenly between all trailers.
Place the heaviest trailer directly behind the cab.
Place the heaviest trailer at the rear.
The trailer weight does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place the heaviest trailer directly behind the cab.
questions.explanation: Put the heaviest trailer closest to the tractor. Put the lightest trailer at the rear.

questions.question: What is the trailer hand valve used for?

options.text: To test the trailer brakes.
To check the connection between the trailer and tractor.
To speed up.
To test the trailer lights.

questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve is used to test the trailer brakes. Use it only for testing.

questions.question: When will an automatic tractor protection valve pop out?

options.text: When air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi.
When the trailer jackknifes.
When wheels regain traction after a skid.
When air pressure is above 45 psi.

questions.correctAnswerText: When air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi.
questions.explanation: The automatic tractor protection valve pops out when air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. This closes the valve and stops air flow.

questions.question: When backing up to couple a trailer, how should you position the tractor?

options.text: At a 90-degree angle in front of the trailer.
Directly in front of the trailer.
At a 30-degree angle in front of the trailer.
At a 60-degree angle in front of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Directly in front of the trailer.
questions.explanation: Back up directly in front of the trailer. Backing at an angle can move the trailer and break the landing gear.

questions.question: What does a tractor protection valve do?

options.text: It keeps air in the brake system if there is a serious leak.
It prevents the truck from being stolen.
It prevents the driver from going too fast.
It prevents the trailer from being accidentally released.

questions.correctAnswerText: It keeps air in the brake system if there is a serious leak.
questions.explanation: The tractor protection valve keeps air in the tractor brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a leak.

questions.question: What happens when only one axle has ABS?

options.text: Braking does not change.
This is not possible.
The driver has better control when braking.
The other axles experience extra strain.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver has better control when braking.
questions.explanation: Having ABS on just one axle or trailer still gives the driver better control when braking.

questions.question: What should you do after finishing a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Close the service line valve.
Remove the service line valve.
Leave the emergency line valve open.
Leave the rear shut-off valves open.

questions.explanation: During inspection, open the rear emergency and service line valves to check for air leaks. Close both valves before you start driving.

questions.question: What happens if you use the trailer hand valve while driving?

options.text: It helps you turn safely.
It stops your trailer safely.
It can cause your trailer to skid.
It is impossible to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can cause your trailer to skid.
questions.explanation: Never use the trailer hand valve while driving. It can cause your trailer to skid.

questions.question: If the trailer begins to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Release the brakes.
Speed up.
Turn the steering wheel quickly left, then right.
Brake harder.

questions.explanation: When your trailer skids, release the brakes. This helps the wheels grip the road again. Once they grip, the trailer will straighten out and follow the truck.

questions.question: How do you check that air reaches all trailers before driving?

options.text: Open the rear shut-off valves and listen for escaping air.
Close the rear shut-off valves and listen for escaping air.
Disconnect air supply lines and listen for escaping air.
Roll each trailer down a hill and test the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open the rear shut-off valves and listen for escaping air.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, open the shut-off valves on the rear of the last trailer. Wait for air pressure to build, then send air to the brakes. If you hear air escaping from the rear valves, air is reaching all trailers.

questions.question: If a trailer begins to skid, what should the driver do?

options.text: Lock the brakes.
Release the brakes.
Steer in the opposite direction.
Speed up.

questions.explanation: If your trailer skids while braking, release the brakes. Let the wheels grip the road again. Once they grip, the trailer will straighten out and follow the truck.

questions.question: What is the trailer hand valve used for?

options.text: It should always be used for parking.
It should only be used for parking downhill.
It should never be used for parking.
It should only be used when carrying cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: It should never be used for parking.
questions.explanation: Never use the trailer hand valve for parking. It can cause all air to leak out of the brake system, and the brakes will release. Use the parking brake instead.

questions.question: What does the emergency air line do?

options.text: It is controlled by the foot brake.
It is connected to the relay valves.
It supplies air to the trailer air tanks.
It prevents skids.

questions.correctAnswerText: It supplies air to the trailer air tanks.
questions.explanation: The emergency air line (also called the supply line) has two jobs. It supplies air to the trailer air tanks and controls the emergency brakes.

questions.question: In what year did newly made trailers first need to have ABS?
questions.explanation: All trailers and converter dollies made on or after March 1, 1998 must have anti-lock braking systems (ABS).

questions.question: How do loaded rigs compare to empty rigs when it comes to rollover risk?

options.text: They are less likely to roll over.
They are more likely to roll over.
They are just as likely to roll over.
They should not be driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are more likely to roll over.
questions.explanation: Loaded rigs have a higher center of gravity because of the cargo weight. This makes them 10 times more likely to roll over in a crash than empty rigs.

questions.question: What happens if you don't grease the fifth wheel plate?

options.text: The trailer could disconnect.
It could cause steering problems.
It could cause braking problems.
It could affect the lights.

questions.explanation: If the fifth wheel plate is not lubricated, friction builds between the truck and trailer. This friction causes steering problems.

questions.question: Which shut-off valves should be open during a trip?

options.text: All shut-off valves should be open.
The rear shut-off valves should be open.
All shut-off valves should be open except the ones on the rear trailer.
No shut-off valves should be open.

questions.correctAnswerText: All shut-off valves should be open except the ones on the rear trailer.
questions.explanation: When starting a trip, open all shut-off valves except the ones on the rear trailer. This ensures air reaches all brake systems and does not escape from the back of the vehicle.

questions.question: What happens if the emergency air line loses pressure?

options.text: The suspension springs extend.
The tractor protection valve opens.
The rear trailer detaches.
The emergency brakes activate.

questions.explanation: The emergency air line controls the emergency brakes. If it loses air pressure, the emergency trailer brakes will activate.
